summary: CCC-era 1933 Aermotor MC-39 lookout near Cloudcroft, NM, with a restored cabin; NRHP-listed 1988. Tower closed to the public, reached on foot.

facts.design: Aermotor MC-39 steel tower, 80 ft, with a 7x7 ft steel cab; wood-frame observer's cabin (1933) and storage shed (1937)

access.note: Tower closed to the public; site reached on foot. Cabin and shed restored in 2012 for a planned public rental, described as soon to open in the Feb 2025 Forest Service update

visit.trail_note: Foot access to the site only; the tower itself is closed to the public

events.note: September 1932 newspaper item reports new steel towers replacing worn-out wooden ones, Wofford among them
Feb 9, 1933 shipment notice for an 80-ft steel tower for Wofford; Feb 16, 1933 notice that it had arrived
Aermotor MC-39 steel tower erected with CCC help by June 1933; NHLR, Wikipedia and the Forest Service all give 1933
Tower and cabin remodeled and improved, per a notice that spells the name Woolford
Henry Beebe moved up to the Wofford tower as fire-control work started early that season
Added to the National Register of Historic Places on January 28, 1988 as part of a thematic group of Southwestern Region lookouts
Observer's cabin and storage shed restored in preparation for cabin rental

corrections.why: The Forest Service page says access to the tower itself is closed to the public and the site is reached on foot; only the cabin rental was expected to open.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR, Wikipedia and the Forest Service date the tower to 1933. A September 1932 item already called the new steel towers placed and an October 1932 item gave an 85-foot height; the February and June 1933 notices and the 80-foot figure in the register and Forest Service pages were preferred.
Newspaper notices give different directions (north, east) and distances (two to four or five miles) from Cloudcroft. The story says only near Cloudcroft.
A 1938 notice spells the lookout Woolford, which the story notes as a spelling in the source.

notes_for_editor: Current status rests on a Forest Service page last updated Feb 19, 2025; the cabin rental opening was not confirmed. The brief's access value was corrected from public to restricted. The MPS nomination (NRHP 64000046) and a recreation.gov listing were not read. No notable fire at this site was found in the sources read.
